title: Standard human oxygen dissociation curve points
source: Wikipedia and Deranged Physiology for P50, LITFL and FPnotebook for saturation at PO2, Europe PMC abstract of Severinghaus JW, J Appl Physiol 1979;46:599-602 for accuracy. The Severinghaus paper itself is behind a subscription and did not open.
rows: Healthy adult; Deranged Physiology gives the normal adult range 24-28 mmHg and cites Brandis for 26.6

Deranged Physiology states the standard conditions as pH 7.40, pCO2 40 mmHg, no dyshaemoglobins; no page opened states the temperature (37 C is the usual standard, not read from a page). Wikipedia: 'typically about 26.6 mmHg (3.5 kPa)'.
'In the adult, the normal p50 should be 24-28mmHg.'
LITFL table pairs 27 mmHg with 50%; FPnotebook the same.
LITFL table row 75% at 40 mmHg. FPnotebook has no 40 mmHg row.
LITFL gives 92% at 60 mmHg; FPnotebook gives 91% at 60 mmHg (92% at 64). The two pages differ by one point.

No page lists 100 mmHg directly. FPnotebook rows: 96% at 90 mmHg and 97% at 110 mmHg ('unreliable above 97%'), so 100 mmHg lies between them; LITFL gives 97% at 95 mmHg. A bracket from neighbouring rows, not a stated point.
Severinghaus (1979) equation fit to the standard curve
Modified Hill equation fitted to standard human blood data, for 0 < S < 1
Abstract: fits 'to within plus or minus 0.0055 fractional saturation (S) from O less than S less than 1'. Another page notes it fits better than the Hill equation below about 30 mmHg.
